_about: Turn animations, measured per monster through the viewer's own clipFor -- the clip it PLAYS, retargeted onto the model by global bone id, NOT the raw motion file (node 00 is in another basis there and reads over 100 degrees out). NOTHING HERE IS CARRIED BETWEEN MONSTERS: list/motion numbers identify a slot on one monster only, so every row is measured from that monster's own animation. A turn animation is the BODY turning while the engine carries the heading, so node 00 leans out and comes home: net under 15 degrees, under 120 frames, and travel under 2 metres (without that a walk or a charge comes through -- Rathian's Motion[7]_loop travels 16.8m). `deg` is THE LONGEST SWING, taken to its extreme. Not the first: a turn clip winds up before it turns, and Rathian's Motion[10] runs +12 for three samples then -20 for seven -- Raven, 2026-09-28: 'L0M10 turns to her right, but she rotates to her left', the viewer having followed the wind-up. Not the biggest either: that made Seregios' Motion[35] and Motion[36] lean the same way when they mirror. POSITIVE IS THE MONSTER'S LEFT, negative its right, confirmed against Rathian's Motion[10] on screen. A lean over 25 degrees stands alone; a gentler one is kept only if another clip of the same list and length leans the other way (`pair`) -- no threshold separates Rathian's 17-20 degree turns from Seregios' 17.8 degree idle sway, but a turn has a mirror and an idle does not. THE LABEL IS STILL THE VIEWER'S, NOT THE ROM'S: the ROM's own mark for a turn is in the action layer and is not read, and mirrored pairs also exist for reactions such as stuns, which this cannot tell apart.
